summary: Online baseline pressure review for the rev0116 work session. These sources sharpen the next executable gates and timing baseline bracket; they are not CloudtainerML evidence until reproduced by this cube.
speculative_conclusion: The riskiest wasted path is continuing to add registry or doctrine layers while the live trace/handoff path is stale or absent. The plausible technical win, if any, must be workload-bound and compared against modern exact dense, KV paging, attention sink, heavy-hitter, and dynamic sparse baselines.

sources.title: FlexAttention + FlashAttention-4: Fast and Flexible
sources.pressure_on_cube: Custom sparse/flexible masks are no longer enough; the cube must show exact semantics plus compiler/kernel-grade execution pressure, or explicitly stay in verifier/product mode.

sources.title: FlexAttention Part II: FlexAttention for Inference
sources.pressure_on_cube: Paged/decoding-oriented attention support means a sparse selector must be compared against runtime-aware baselines, not only dense math fixtures.

sources.title: vLLM project site and repository
sources.pressure_on_cube: Serving systems attack latency through KV paging, scheduling, batching, graph execution, and memory management; CloudtainerML should make a named-hardware baseline bracket mandatory.

sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
sources.pressure_on_cube: KV memory waste is a first-class baseline; sparse reads are not enough if paging and batching dominate end-to-end performance.

sources.title: FlashAttention-3: Fast and Accurate Attention with Asynchrony and Low-precision
sources.pressure_on_cube: Exact dense attention is a moving target on modern GPUs; any sparse claim must compare against IO-aware kernels on named hardware.

sources.title: MInference 1.0: Accelerating Pre-filling for Long-Context LLMs via Dynamic Sparse Attention
sources.pressure_on_cube: Sparse long-context acceleration exists in stronger forms; this cube needs hostile comparisons and workload boundaries, not generic sparse wins.

sources.title: H2O: Heavy-Hitter Oracle for Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models
sources.pressure_on_cube: The right comparison may be a KV retention policy, not a score sparsity policy. Decode-phase memory traffic is a central risk.

sources.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks
sources.pressure_on_cube: Attention-sink plus window baselines can preserve behavior with bounded cache; generated-token/decode tests matter more than prefill-only fixtures.
